comparison_note: Different model architectures and initialization histories; this is not an isolated warmstart ablation.

interface.loop: RGB views + proprioception + instruction + robot schema + history -> model reasoning -> one strict JSON action -> deterministic controller -> new observation
interface.contract: Each adapter fixes allowed action type, arm names, frames, units, joint ordering, gripper/hand coordinates, bounds and action duration. Full robot-specific semantics; identical parser and observations for both models.
interface.bimanual: Both arms are included in the same synchronized action record; Allegro hands use explicit finger joints.
interface.reasoning_tasks: Reasoning followed by typed JSON answer: point/set/label/count/pose/prediction. Active perception can issue permitted observation actions before its answer.
interface.policy_inputs: Public RGB/proprioception/calibration and declared robot specification only; simulator labels and reset state stay in the generator/grader.
interface.execution: Deterministic IK/control and schema validation only; no task-level planner, code execution, skill library or teacher action repair.

control_training.scope: Nine EFE candidate families plus the full native GR00T YAM catalog. This replaces the earlier five-family-only proposal.
control_training.count_meaning: Eligible frozen training inventory, not implemented adapters or training admission; counts exclude native GR00T YAM.

selection.libero-max: 50 candidate variants, 23 semantic tasks; preserve protected scenes.
selection.robocasa: Select 8 complementary tasks from 22 candidates; keep this a small kitchen subset.
selection.robodojo: Start general_pickup and align_blocks, then select 8-12 stacking, sorting, placement and language-directed tasks from 34 candidates.
selection.abc-sim: 23 dual-YAM candidates; prioritize transfer, reorientation, coordinated object handling, then count/spell instruction tasks.
selection.dexjoco: 3 training bimanual tasks: assembly, Hanoi, microwave cooking. Support the 16 Allegro joint targets per hand explicitly.
selection.robolab: 38 native language-goal candidates; use existing left/right, spatial and specified-order tasks with their original instructions and verifiers.
selection.vlabench: 27 candidates for semantic, spatial, ordinal and commonsense object selection and physical questions.
selection.yamlab: 6 candidate scenes of mug hanging and pot placement; distinct from native GR00T YAM.

control_training.other_scene_sources_note: Reasoning-scene providers initially; added only when independent scenes, required labels and allowed runtime are available.

families.name: Object referring and pointing
families.training_environment: Procedural tabletop and room scenes; qualified training scenes from RoboCasa, MolmoSpaces, VLABench, RoboLab and YAMLab.
tasks: Point to an object described by category, color, shape, size or visible state.
Disambiguate similar objects using visible relations.
Return no target only when the generated query has no valid referent.
families.example: Point to the small blue cup beside the open drawer.
families.output: One normalized image point, or an explicit no-target response.
families.reward: Point inside the visible instance mask of any valid referent; calibrated no-target correctness. Masks and instance IDs are evaluator-only.

families.name: Set pointing and counting
families.training_environment: Procedural clutter generator with varying categories, counts, occlusion and distractors.
tasks: Point to every instance satisfying an attribute or relation.
Count matching visible instances.
Select the second or third object in an explicitly defined ordering.
families.example: Mark every red fastener outside the tray and report how many there are.
families.output: A set of normalized image points and an integer count.
families.reward: One-to-one matching of points to valid visible instances, set precision/recall and exact count; duplicate points are penalized.

families.name: Spatial relations and reference frames
families.training_environment: Generated scene graphs over qualified MuJoCo and Isaac Sim training scenes, with explicit camera, robot or object reference frames.
tasks: Compose two to four spatial relations to select a referent.
Answer relative depth, distance, orientation and containment queries.
Convert between reference frames whose definition is available to the model.
families.example: From the robot viewpoint, point to the object behind the bowl that is left of the kettle.
families.output: A point, relation label, or numeric answer in a declared coordinate convention.
families.reward: Exact scene-graph predicate evaluation or bounded geometric error; multiple valid answers are accepted and ambiguous prompts are filtered.

families.name: Placement and packing
families.training_environment: Procedurally cluttered counters, trays, drawers, shelves and containers in qualified training scenes.
tasks: Choose free space satisfying language constraints.
Account for the placed object footprint and orientation.
Place inside, between or beside targets while avoiding collisions and unsupported locations.
families.example: Place this box between the bottle and bowl, entirely on the shelf.
families.output: Placement point or pose; optional subsequent native robot action episode.
families.reward: Collision-free full footprint, support, containment and relation predicates, with physics settling where appropriate; a pixel in empty space alone is insufficient.

families.name: Cross-view correspondence
families.training_environment: Paired and multi-view renders of the same independently generated training scene, with known geometry and camera calibration in the grader.
tasks: Locate the same surface point or object part in another view.
Match identities through viewpoint change, occlusion and distractors.
Report that the reference point is not visible when appropriate.
families.example: Find the marked drawer-handle tip in the wrist-camera image.
families.output: A target-view image point, or explicit not-visible response.
families.reward: Visibility-checked 3D reprojection and surface/instance identity with normalized pixel tolerance; no arbitrary choice between symmetric valid matches.

families.name: Affordances and object parts
families.training_environment: Procedural articulated cabinets, containers, knobs, handles and tools from an audited training asset registry.
tasks: Point to the part needed for opening, pressing, grasping or turning.
Choose a contact point and direction.
Select a tool or grasp compatible with a stated operation.
families.example: Where should the gripper contact this cabinet to pull the door open?
families.output: Point and optional contact direction or operation label.
families.reward: Annotated part geometry plus analytic feasibility or simulated operation success; dataset semantics must be specified independently of benchmark answers.

families.name: Physical prediction and counterfactuals
families.training_environment: Short deterministic branches of generated MuJoCo or qualified Isaac Sim training scenes.
tasks: Predict which object moves, falls or becomes accessible after a stated intervention.
Determine whether an object fits through an opening or a drawer can open.
Choose a stable placement or a nonblocking action order.
families.example: Which block falls if the support beneath it is removed?
families.output: Object point, outcome label, pose or short action ordering.
families.reward: Agreement with branched simulator outcomes or geometric constraints; required physical properties must be visible, stated or discoverable by permitted probes.

families.name: Active perception and spatial memory
families.training_environment: Multi-turn generated training scenes with allowed camera moves and controlled object motion or temporary occlusion.
tasks: Choose a view that reveals the target.
Track an object or relation across observed motion and occlusion.
Gather sufficient visual evidence, then answer a grounding or placement query.
families.example: Inspect the other side of the tray, then point to the cup that was moved there.
families.output: Permitted view actions followed by a grounded answer.
families.reward: Final verifiable answer with a bounded observation/action budget; never reward guesses about unseen random changes.

scene_sources: New procedural tabletop and room scenes rendered with MuJoCo, optional Blender rendering, and qualified Isaac Sim adapters.
Only scene identities already admitted to training from the existing candidate simulator suites.
Audited training-only object, part, material and texture assets.
reasoning_training.label_source: Scene geometry, object identity, visibility, camera transforms and simulator outcomes. No benchmark annotations or benchmark-derived teacher answers.
reasoning_training.model_inputs: RGB observations, task text, and declared camera/robot state or allowed interaction feedback. Hidden simulator state is accessible only to generation and grading.
reasoning_training.task_counts: Eight generator/adapter families, not eight fixed tasks. Seeds, resets, camera views and paraphrases do not count as new semantic tasks.

exclusions: Benchmark images, videos, scans, scene IDs, annotations and instructions.
Crops, rerenders of the same held-out scene, paraphrases, and teacher-generated answers derived from held-out inputs.
Benchmark rewards or scores for curriculum adaptation, hyperparameter tuning, early stopping or checkpoint selection.
holdouts.development: Use independent development scenes, asset/scene groups and generator combinations. Keep named benchmark evaluation isolated from selection.
identity_checks: Scene, asset and capture ancestry separation
No render of a protected scene through another camera
holdouts.foundation_model_note: This controls the new training data only; prior exposure of pretrained or warmstarted checkpoints to these benchmarks has not been established.

data_scale_proposal.control_note: Only count distinct physically valid generated configurations. Native fixed scenes require a separate training generator; do not relabel repeated seeds as new scenes.
data_scale_proposal.splits: Existing protected splits remain fixed. New training/dev/test scenes are separated by scene and asset groups; new semantic task holdouts are frozen before sampling.
data_scale_proposal.language: Use existing benchmarks/environments and their native instructions, goals, variants and success checks: RoboLab, VLABench, LIBERO-Max, RoboDojo and ABC-Sim, plus existing native GR00T YAM language tasks. Select only allowed training membership. No new synthetic instruction pairs, generated paraphrase corpus or modified goal predicates for this component.
data_scale_proposal.reasoning_bank_note: The 200,000-pair figure is proposed generator/pool capacity; report unique scenes and queries actually sampled separately. It is not a claim that every pair is trained on.

optimizer.algorithm: PEAR GRPO with zero-variance group filtering and score-centered REINFORCE bypass loss
optimizer.long_sequence_gate: Model context and full-model numerical/memory checks; record actual truncation per family.
optimizer.reasoning_budget_note: Development-driven proposals; distinguish total episode budget from tokens per action. No length reward.

multitask_balancing.initial_phase: First 32 updates use fixed bucket targets and family loss weights; same rules for both arms.
multitask_balancing.post_filter: Enforce retained-group quotas after constant-reward filtering, with bounded acceptance-aware refill. Log all attempts and failures. Do not silently fill deficits with faster tasks.
multitask_balancing.loss: L = 0.75 * sum_control(w_k * mean_generated_token_PEAR_SC_loss_k) + 0.25 * sum_reasoning(v_k * mean_generated_token_PEAR_SC_loss_k); w and v each sum to one.
multitask_balancing.loss_note: Family token denominators are global across ranks. This is an intentional change from PEAR global token-mean reduction. Sampling quotas must not cause a second multiplication by the same family weight.
multitask_balancing.adaptive_phase: After update 32, bounded MT-GRPO-inspired weight changes every 16 updates using complete training-probe successes and per-family pre/post surrogate improvement. Hyperparameters calibrated on independent development only.
multitask_balancing.adaptation_limits: Keep total control 96 and reasoning 32. Cap changes to 20% relative per adaptation; maintain rolling coverage of every admitted simulator and task. Same algorithm and initial weights; model-specific histories are recorded.
multitask_balancing.no_signal: Differentiate all-success, all-failure, invalid actions and infrastructure failure; infrastructure outcomes do not enter rewards or success estimates.
multitask_balancing.objective_note: These are engineering defaults, not a proven optimal mix. Equal reward ranges do not ensure equal gradients; audit gradient norms and conflicts.

sgs.status: Restartable sampling state and native PEAR trainer hooks implemented; reset banks and GPU integration validation remain pending.
sgs.scope: Choose a reset stratum (full start / grasped / near goal) under explicit quotas, then a configuration within the semantic task, before drawing 8 fresh policy rollouts.
sgs.our_extension: Mix 20% uniform configurations with 80% SGS weights. Use a smoothed cold-start estimate; history includes every valid rollout, including filtered groups. Keep arm-specific histories and sampler versions.
sgs.reset_curriculum: Native full starts, valid grasped-object starts and nonterminal near-goal starts. Begin at least 50% full-start groups per task and expand to at least 75% during consolidation. Only use audited physically stable states allowed by the training verifier.
sgs.no_signal_limit: If every reset fails, SGS has no frontier to identify; add reachable intermediate reset configurations or easier subproblems. Never supply a hidden solution to the policy.
sgs.evaluation: Native/full-start performance is primary; assisted-start success reported separately. Frozen evaluation distributions, never SGS-selected.
sgs.interaction_with_grpo: For binary independent rollouts, P(group retained)=1-p^8-(1-p)^8. The resulting training configuration distribution also depends on this filter, so log raw and retained reset distributions.
sgs.test: Short matched pilot branches using uniform resets versus SGS from the same checkpoint, same reset bank, reward, token allowance and GPU budget. Measure full-start success plus retained groups per GPU-hour.
sgs.limitation: SGS was tested with PPO and different actor observations/training; its benefit for reasoning VLM GRPO is a hypothesis.
sgs.sparse_history: Use shrinking success estimates for sparse control configurations; H=100 is the maximum window, not a prerequisite. For procedurally generated reasoning, estimate learnability at generator/template/difficulty-bin level, rather than requiring repeated trials for each unique image.
sgs.near_goal_guard: Exclude already-successful starts and physically invalid states. Do not reset into memory tasks without the corresponding observable history. Near-goal training changes the reset distribution and is tracked separately from full-start training.

stages.purpose: Fixed multitask mixture; verify learning, full-start success, task coverage and throughput. Measure throughput after 2-4 updates.
Expand catalog and reset diversity; enable qualified SGS and bounded multitask reweighting.
Conditional on development gains and measured cost: harder compositions, full-start transfer and retention.

schedule.scale_rule: Use admitted semantic tasks, retained-group exposure, unique attempted reset/scene coverage, and per-family full-start training/development success to determine continuation. 512 is a planning milestone, not a guarantee of learning or a fixed endpoint. Any longer schedule remains a proposal while paused.

coverage_budget.interpretation: Necessary exposure lower bound under fixed bucket quotas, not a convergence theorem. SGS resampling, repeated configurations and changing quotas require direct measurement.
coverage_budget.example_note: Assumes all 210 candidate EFE semantic tasks are admitted and an even aggregate allocation. Per-bucket bottlenecks can require more updates. Eight rollouts in a group share the initial configuration; they are not eight distinct scenes.
coverage_signals: attempted and retained groups per semantic task
native full-start success on training probes
coverage_budget.solved_tasks: Do not chase retained-group targets on already mastered tasks whose groups have zero variance; use success evidence and periodic retention probes.

conditional_extension.condition: Expanded admitted task count or measured undercoverage warrants continuation, development improves, and measured compute cost is acceptable.

diagnostic_actions.train_and_dev_low_with_all_failure_group: Fix exploration/reset curriculum or interface and horizon before extending blindly.
diagnostic_actions.train_improves_dev_improves: Continue updates while checking per-task exposure.
diagnostic_actions.train_high_dev_low: Increase distinct training scenes and task compositions supported by the existing benchmark; repeated optimization alone is not the fix.
diagnostic_actions.one_family_regresses: Inspect task/loss balance and gradient interference; adjust bounded weights and retention coverage.
diagnostic_actions.persistent_underfit_with_useful_signal_a: Investigate optimization, representation and parameter capacity; do not assume a larger model is required from diversity alone.

compute.expansion: Target 16 H100 nodes per arm: 2 trainer, 12 rollout and 2 simulator nodes. Start with one-node model checks, then measure throughput before assigning primary roles. Up to 16 nodes per scheduler job and 34 nodes across the study; these are authorized limits, not allocated capacity.
compute.cost_note: The published PEAR run reports about 50,000 H100-equivalent GPU-hours. This broader two-arm ceiling is a large research budget, not an overnight ETA; estimate costs from the pilot before committing to completion.

primary: native language-task success and instruction adherence
evaluation.selection: Independent development only. Named held-out benchmarks are final reports, not curriculum signals.
evaluation.comparison: Same task registry and evaluation seeds, full-FT policy, reward and sampler rules. Report both learning versus retained exposure and versus GPU-hours. This is a two-system comparison; it does not isolate warmstart from architecture.

holdout_review.status: frozen membership; seen/unseen labels remain provisional until actual training and scene ancestry audit
holdout_review.scene_verification: The three core same-task/new-variant candidates have variant_scene_verified=false. Do not report them as independently verified unseen scenes yet.

lineage_check.limit: Task-ID check on the warmstart candidate superset, not a complete scene/asset ancestry or earlier-checkpoint audit.

rules: Keep development separate from final test. Training curriculum uses training probes; no final-test feedback for adaptation or checkpoint selection.
Define unseen simulator using all new training exposure, including reasoning-scene generators and warmstart ancestry; rendering its scenes makes that simulator seen.
Recompute seen-task versus new-task cohorts from actual admitted task families and equivalent goal definitions, not task directory names alone.
Native GR00T YAM: use existing test split if present; otherwise freeze semantic task families and scene/asset groups before rollout generation. The full catalog is still required.
SAPIEN is an unseen runtime, not an unseen physics engine when Isaac/PhysX has been trained; Genesis can be held out at both levels.
Same constrained action interface for every arm; do not score unsupported adapters or infrastructure failures as model failures.
